title: AI advisory
audience: For CXOs, founders, and heads of engineering
description: Where AI actually fits in your business, what to build and what to buy, and which workflows are worth making agentic first. I still build and ship AI products myself, so the advice comes from inside the work rather than from a deck.
points: An unbiased read on vendors and where your money is going
Which parts of your operations are worth making agentic first
Advice from someone still shipping agents in production
label: How advisory works

title: Tech coaching
description: Working with your team on how they build — TDD, BDD, clean code, continuous delivery — and fixing the problem rather than the symptom. These practices matter more now as AI is writing most of the code, not less.
points: Working alongside your team, not presenting at them
The practices that keep quality up as the pace goes up
Habits that stay after I leave
label: How coaching works

title: 1:1 mentoring
audience: For engineering leaders and senior engineers
description: Regular sessions to unblock your teams and think through the calls you’re not sure about. Bring whatever is actually bothering you — an agent that keeps going sideways, a roadmap you want a second opinion on, a team that has quietly stopped reviewing what the model writes.
points: Roadmap and agent-programme reviews between sessions
Practical guidance on tools, patterns, and guardrails
Direct feedback on what your teams are building
label: How mentoring works

title: AI workshops
description: A few days with your engineers, working in your own codebase instead of a demo project. They leave knowing how to test and review AI-written code — the way I wrote it up in Test-First Copilot, taught to real teams since.
points: Live coding in your real codebase, on your stack
Test-first patterns that hold when an agent writes the code
Quality guardrails for review, CI, and merging agent output
label: What a workshop covers
